title: platform-as-inference-strategy-brief
body:
One-pager: Platform-as-Inference — strategic brief for a builders-first narrative

Context and intent:
This brief is intended for product marketing, field enablement, and solutions teams who need a concise, operational narrative that explains why teams should choose Redwood for production LLM features. It tilts away from model-only conversations and toward the economic, reliability, and developer-producibility benefits of treating inference as a first-class platform. Use this as the canonical short-form message for decks, sales calls, and field one-pagers.

Core thesis (short)
As open model ecosystems proliferate, the differentiator moves from model access to serving: predictable latency, unit economics, and operational simplicity at scale. Teams win when they standardize on an inference platform that makes performance and cost repeatable across environments. Redwood is built to be that platform.

Mission (candidate wording)
Make industrial-grade LLM inference routine for product teams — predictable performance, cost, and control across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Why this matters (elevator logic)
- Models keep changing; serving constraints don’t.
- Poor inference economics (latency spikes, token waste, cold-cache costs) translate directly into broken products or unsustainable bills.
- Developers want an API and workflow that maps to shipping features, not infrastructure wrestling.

One-line value proposition
Redwood delivers predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference so engineering teams can ship conversational and generative features with production SLAs and minimal ops overhead.

Four strategic pillars (messaging anchors)
1) Economic predictability: measurable per-token economics via batching, cache primitives, and model routing so teams can forecast and control bill shocks.
2) Production reliability: fallbacks, regional routing, and SLA-backed capacity to keep features online under load or model churn.
3) Developer-first experience: consistent API, SDKs, and observability that let engineers treat models as product components rather than ephemeral experiments.
4) Deployment flexibility: same operational surface for hosted APIs, reserved (dedicated) capacity, and private installs for regulated workloads.

Segmented proof points (quick lines for SDRs/sellers)
- AI-native startups: Ship fast with hosted API + auto-scaling; reduce dev time to MLP by 60% vs. self-managed infra (internal case study #GTM-5).
- Mid-market product teams: predictable monthly inference spend using dedicated capacity; 95th percentile latency SLAs and token-level cost dashboards.
- Regulated enterprises: private control plane + KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs to satisfy SOC/ISO audits.

Competitive posture (how to differentiate quickly)
- Against managed cloud AI endpoints: emphasize predictable unit economics and runtime optimizations (batching, KV cache) that cloud endpoints leave as infra exercises.
- Against model-access APIs: flip the question from "which model" to "how do we serve reliably and affordably"; show routing/fallbacks and observability as mission-critical.
- Against open-source self-hosted runtimes: tradeoff map — faster time-to-value and multi-tenant economics vs building your own orchestration and monitoring. Redwood combines runtime performance with operational primitives so teams don't reimplement core serving concerns.

Proof points and measurable claims (short)
- Average production token cost reduction: 30%–55% from batching + prefix caching on real workloads (internal evals).
- 99.9% regional uptime for Dedicated customers in last quarter (SRE metrics).
- Onboard time to POC (hosted API): <72 hours with sample app and SDK.

Elevator pitch variations (30s)
- Developer-first product lead: "Redwood is the inference runtime that makes LLM features predictable — fast SDKs, cost dashboards, and SLAs so your team can ship without guessing at latency or cost."
- Platform lead / CTO: "Instead of debating models, standardize on a serving layer that guarantees throughput and cost — Redwood gives you a single control plane for hosted, dedicated, and private inference."

Objections and succinct rebuttals
- "We can just host models ourselves." — Rebuttal: Hosting is the start; scaling predictable economics, routing variants, and long-term observability are a non-trivial operational tax. Redwood surfaces that work with repeatable guardrails.
- "We need full control for compliance." — Rebuttal: Redwood Private provides a customer-managed control plane and on-prem options with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; we can map to compliance needs without losing runtime benefits.
- "Open models are free; why pay?" — Rebuttal: Model weights are only one cost; inference efficiency, engineering time, and reliability gaps create the biggest ongoing expense. Redwood reduces those variable costs with runtime features and tooling.

Key tactical calls to action for GTM
- Run an ROI micro-case for three target accounts (one from each segment) to generate quantifiable token savings and latency improvements; deliver a short two-slide ROI + one-pager for field sellers. Link: JIRA GTM-241.
- Create a one-click demo flow for hosted API that highlights caching impact on a noisy real-world prompt set (embed sample app in Quickstart).
- Field collateral: 30-second video + two two-pagers (developer & CTO variants).

Open questions / risks for leadership
- Do we want a publicized "unit-economics benchmark" public report or keep metrics gated for sales conversations? (Ops and legal need to sign off on published methodology.)
- How aggressive should price tiers be for Dedicated reservations vs. hosted volume discounts? (Finance modelling required.)

Recommended next steps (owners + timeline)
- GTM: finalize two-pager variants and elevator scripts — owner: Marco Alvarez — due: 2025-03-12.
- Product: finalize messaging on batching/cache primitives and add a short technical note for sales engineers — owner: Evelyn Park — due: 2025-03-08.
- Growth: build ROI micro-case template and instrument the Quickstart demo flow — owner: Lydia Chen — due: 2025-03-20.

Notes and references
- Related artifacts: Confluence strategy draft (linked above), runtime perf PR (github link), ROI JIRA (GTM-241).
- Tone guidance: avoid heavy model marketing language; lead with economics, reliability, and developer productivity.
